reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that a dense Al2O3 layer improves oxidation resistance in Ti-45Al-8.5Nb alloys at 1000 °C, but it does not address ALD deposition, the HfNbTaTiZr composition, or the preservation of mechanical properties. The key premises about ALD applicability, mechanical property retention, and transferability to a different alloy system are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: A ~50 nm ALD Al2O3 coating can form a continuous, dense, and adherent barrier on a refractory high-entropy alloy.
An Al2O3 layer limits oxygen diffusion and reduces oxidation at 1000 °C.
The coating will not degrade the alloy's room- and high-temperature mechanical properties.
The cited evidence on TiAl intermetallics is directly transferable to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
